A prediction log looks like a stable object. You query it, you get numbers, the numbers move when the model changes. That is the story you tell yourself.
Here is the same table, read honestly. ai_predictions holds 48,737 rows written between 2026-06-21 and 2026-11-21, across 130 columns. Eight of those columns have never held a single value. Forty-four were born after the first row was inserted. Eleven stopped being written before this month began.
Every one of those facts changes what a WHERE clause means, and none appear in the query you wrote six weeks ago.
All counts are from production, not an example schema.
Postgres knows which columns exist. It does not know when each one started carrying data, or whether it still does. That is one pass over the catalog plus one aggregate per colum…

articles.author: Jashwanti Bhandai
articles.description:
Many factories, warehouses and logistics fleets already have sensors. Fewer have a clear way to use what those sensors collect. Dashboards fill up with numbers, and teams still make decisions by instinct. The gap is rarely the hardware. It is the step between raw data and action.
Combining the Internet of Things (IoT) with AI closes that gap.
What each side contributes
IoT supplies the signal: temperature, vibration, location, energy use, machine status and more, streamed from devices in the field.
AI supplies the interpretation. It can spot patterns a person would miss, flag unusual readings and predict problems before they happen.
On their own, sensors tell you what happened. Together with AI, the system can tell you what is likely to happen next and what to do about it.
Practical use cases
Devices and connectivity. Sensors and gateways that send reliable data, even on poor networks.
Data pipeline. A way to clean, store and organize readings. Poor data quality is the most common reason these projects stall.
Models. Anomaly detection, forecasting or vision models, matched to the actual decision you want to improve.
Edge versus cloud. Some decisions, such as stopping a machine, need to happen locally in milliseconds. Others, such as weekly trend analysis, suit the cloud. Most real systems use both.
Action layer. Alerts, work orders or automated responses that reach the people who can act.
How to avoid a stalled pilot
IoT gives you the data, and AI makes it useful. The companies that benefit most don't start with the biggest deployment. They pick one costly problem, prove value quickly, and scale what works.
About the author: This article was written by the team at Movenetics Digital, which develops AI-powered IoT solutions that connect devices, collect real-time data and automate monitoring.
articles.title: IoT and AI Together: How to Turn Device Data into Better Decisions

articles.author: Lyra
articles.description:
Every hand-built Linux image eventually grows the same wart: a shell script that pipes commands into sfdisk, calls partprobe, runs resize2fs, and hopes the device really was /dev/sda.
It works exactly once. Change the disk, add a partition, or boot the same image on a board that enumerates storage differently, and the script either fails halfway or, worse, succeeds against the wrong device. The deeper problem is that the script encodes positions. What you actually mean is "this disk should have a swap partition and a root partition that fills the rest."
systemd-repart is the declarative version of that idea. You write small .conf files describing the partitions that should exist, and the tool makes the partition table match. It is incremental by design: existing partitions are matched by t…
articles.title: Stop Partitioning Disks by Hand: Practical systemd-repart on Linux

import time

Cilium HostFirewall guards node traffic, but it is disabled by default


Cilium's host firewall extends network policy to the Kubernetes node itself. The Cilium Helm reference lists hostFirewall.enabled with a default of false. When it is not enabled, policies aimed at the host endpoint do not provide the node-level enforcement that an operator may expect. A cluster can have detailed pod policies and still allow broad node traffic between hosts, management networks, and workload networks.
Host policies use a CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy with a node selector instead of an endpoint selector. The Cilium documentation describes the host firewall as a way to enforce security policies for Kubernetes nodes.
